Negative Appraisals.value: I can no longer trust my own body
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

issues.item: Intrinsic Fault: There is something about me that made the event happen
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness in a 74-year-old patient, endorsing both strong self-blame for causing the illness and strong guilt for not doing more to stop it is clinically questionable unless there is a very specific illness context. These appraisals are more typical of interpersonal trauma or preventable accidents than of severe illness, so a clinician would likely question whether these items fit this trauma type.

issues.item: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: For life-threatening illness, severe inaction guilt is hard to reconcile unless there was a clear missed-action scenario; with no supporting threat, memory, trigger, or strategy items, this appraisal is clinically difficult to anchor.

issues.item: Lost Community: I have lost my connection to my community and culture
issues.explanation: For a 74-year-old woman with life-threatening illness, 'Body Unreliable' and 'Body as Enemy' form a coherent illness-related appraisal cluster, but 'Lost Community' introduces a different trauma meaning domain without support from any Trigger, Threat, Memory, or Maladaptive Strategies items. Given the formulation has no active edges, the selected node should still be internally coherent on its own; this item is the odd one out and weakly tied to the illness-focused bodily appraisals.
